text: Pehr Löfling (31 January 1729 – 22 February 1756) was a Swedish botanist and a devoted follower of Carl Linnaeus. Born in Tolvfors Bruk, Gävle, Sweden, he studied at the University of Uppsala, where he took courses taught by Linnaeus. When the Spanish ambassador requested Linnaeus to appoint a botanist for service in the American colonies, Linnaeus immediately selected Löfling. Löfling traveled to Spain in 1751 to learn Spanish and then joined a scientific expedition to South America in February 1754. The Treaty of Madrid, signed on 13 January 1750, had established the colonial borders between Spain and Portugal. In Cumaná, Venezuela (then a Spanish colony), Löfling participated in the Expedicion de Limites al Orinoco, a project to demarcate the border with Brazil, and was assigned to lead the natural history department responsible for evaluating the region’s resources. He worked on the expedition with two young Spanish doctors and remained involved throughout his life. Löfling died in a remote mission called San Antonio de Caroni, located on the banks of the Caroní River near the present-day city of Ciudad Guayana, Venezuela. His death was seen as a significant loss to natural history, particularly to botany, and Carl Linnaeus regarded it as irreparable. After his death, his manuscripts were preserved by his two assistants. In 1753, Linnaeus named the genus Loeflingia for plants in the family Caryophyllaceae, one species of which is found in Spain and another in Spanish America. In 1923, Sprague published Pehria, a monotypic genus of plants from South America in the family Lythraceae, also named in honor of Löfling. A park named Parque Löefling in Ciudad Guayana, Venezuela, is dedicated to him and includes a zoo. Linnaeus posthumously published his Iter Hispanicum, eller resa til Spanska Länderna uti Europa och America 1751 til 1756 in 1758.
